βαγώας.definition: Lat. Bagoas and Bagöus, Persian word, said to be = as pr. n. in Str.15.3.24, etc

βάθος.definition: depth or height, acc. as; Astron., = Vett.Val.241.26

βάθρον.definition: that on which anything steps or; stage, scaffold, Hdt.7.23

βαθύτης.definition: = depth, Luc.Icar.5: metaph. of character, Phld.Ir.p.60 W.; of mental profundity, Cic.Att.4.6.3,al

βαίτη.definition: Dor. Sophr.38:—shepherd's or peasant's; tent of skins, S.Fr.1031

βάκχυλος.definition: bread baked in hot ashes, Elean word, Nic.Fr.121

βάλαγρος.definition: a fresh-water fish, prob. a kind of carp, Arist.HA538a15

βάλανος.definition: tree which bears ib.6, Plb.34.8.1, LXXGe.35.8; from similarity of shape

βαλβίς.definition: prop. rope drawn across the race-; since the starting-point was also the goal, was used for any point to be gained, as the battlements , S.Ant.131 , cf. Lyc.287, Opp.C.1.513

βάλερος.definition: or kind of carp, Arist.HA568b27:—also ib.602b26; cf

βάλλις.definition: plant with wonderful medicinal properties, Xanth.16

βάμμα.definition: that in which a thing is

βάραθρος.definition: one that ought to be thrown into the pit, Luc.Pseudol.17

βάραξ.definition: a kind of cake, Epil.3; cf

βαρίβας.definition: one that goes in a boat, S.Fr.517

βάρος.definition: Ion. weight, Hdt.2.73, etc; a weight, burden, load, A.Ch.1000, etc.; S.Fr.945: pl., weights, Arist.Mech.850a30

βᾶρος.definition: or a kind of spice, Mnesim.4.62

βάσιμος.definition: passable, accessible; fixed, stable, Eustr.in EN98.3

βάσσων.definition: gen. Dor. Comp. of Epich.188; baggage-train, Petr.Patr.p.434 D

βάτιον.definition: Dim. of , Salaminian name for mulberry, Parth. ap. Ath.2.51f

βατίς.definition: a flat fish, perh. skate or ray; bird that frequents bushes, possibly stone-chat, ib.592b17

βάτος.definition: bramble, Rubus ulmifolius; raspberry, Rubus Idaeus, Dsc.4.38; = Thphr.HP3.18.4

βάψις.definition: dipping, tempering; a dye, Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19

βέρβερι.definition: pearl-mussel, foreign word, Androsth. ap. Ath.3.93b

βῆμα.definition: Aeol. and Dor. step; step, as a measure of length, = 10 about 2 1/2 feet, HeroDef.131

βῆσσα.definition: Dor. poet. Noun, wooded combe, glen; drinking cup at Alexandria, broader below and narrower above, Ath.11.784b

βῆτα.definition: indecl., the letter Pl.Cra.393e, Arist.Metaph.1087a8, AP11.437 , Luc.Herm.40, etc

βήχιον.definition: colt's-foot, Tussilago Farfara, used to; slight cough, Id.Eup.2.31

βιβλίον.definition: or strip of Thphr.HP4.8.4; = petition to the Government, = Lat. libellus, BGU422 , POxy.86.16 , etc

βικόστομον.definition: opening of a receiving vessel, of a still, Zos.Alch.p.224B

βίοςι.definition: life, i. e. not animal life , but; lifetime, Hdt.6.109; Pl.Phdr.242a, cf. PMagd.18.7 , etc

βίτος.definition: tyre, Edict. Diocl.15.31a:—hence with tyres, ib.34; with tyred wheels, ib.36,37

βλέννα.definition: = mucous discharge, Hp.Mul.1.58 ; of the humour 'phlegm', Prodic.4, etc

βλέψις.definition: sight , Plu.Pel.32; metaph., contemplation, consideration, Epicur.Ep.3p.63U

βλῆμα.definition: throw, cast, of dice; shot, wound, Hdt.3.35, Hp.Prorrh.2.14

βόαμα.definition: Dor. for , shriek, cry, A.Ag.920; loud strain, Lyr.Adesp.102

βοή.definition: Dor. loud cry, shout, in Hom. mostly; = aid called for, succour, A.Supp.730, Ag.1349, S.OC1057 . 'proclaim aloud'.)

βολεών.definition: dunghill, Din. ap. Harp., Philem.221 codd., Nic. ap. Harp., Eust.1404 fin

βολίζη.definition: female slave, Cretan word in Seleuc. ap. Ath.6.267c

βόλιον.definition: counter used in the game of; = Ps.-Dsc.3.110

βόλος.definition: throw with a casting-net, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.62; net, Herod.7.75, Ael.NA8.3; for birds, AP6.184

βόρασσος.definition: growing spadix of the date with immature fruit, Dsc.1.109

βόσμορον.definition: an Indian millet, ragi, Eleusine coracana, Str.15.1.13 and 18:—also Peripl. M. Rubr.14.41

βούβαστις.definition: groin, Aët.4.21:—hence remedies for sores in the groin, ibid

βουλή.definition: Dor. Decr.Byz. ap. D.18.90, Aeol; decree, And.1.61; Id.2.28

βουνίτης.definition: dweller on the hills, of Pan

βοῦτις.definition: or vessel in the shape of the frustum of a cone, HeroStereom.2.9; ib.1.52, Aët.3.133:—Dim. Hippiatr.34

βράβυλος.definition: the tree which bears Aret.CA2.2; seedling peach, Gp.10.13.5

βράγχος.definition: hoarseness or sore throat causing; a disease in swine , Id.HA603a31

βράθυ.definition: savin, Juniperus Sabina, Dsc.1.76; also, = J. foetidissima, ibid

βράσμα.definition: v.l. for Dsc.2.159; shaking motion, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.81

βράστης.definition: of an earthquake, upheaving the earth verlically, Arist.Mu.396a3

βρέγμα.definition: front part of the head, Batr.228; in pl., parietal bones, Gal.17.3

βρένθος.definition: an unknown water-bird, Arist.HA609a23; haughty carriage, arrogance, Ath.13.611e

βρίζα.definition: rye, Secale cereale, in Thrace and Macedonia; Aeol. for A.D.Adv.157.20, Greg.Cor.p.576 S

βρόμος.definition: any loud noise, as the crackling; also (Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.20

βρότος.definition: blood that has run from a wound, gore, in Il. always 7.425, al.; Od.24.189

βρυάκτης.definition: of Pan, the jolly god, Poet. ap. Stob.1.1.30

βρυδαλίχα.definition: female mask; also, lewd woman , Id

βρύον.definition: oyster-green, Ulva Lactuca; tree-moss, Usnea barbata, Theoc.21.7, Dsc.1.21

βρῶμα.definition: that which is eaten, food; cavity in a tooth, Hp.Epid.4.25, Dsc.1.105, Archig. ap. Gal.12.859

βύας.definition: eagle-owl, Strix bubo, Arist.HA592b9 an owl hooted, D.C.56.29, 72.24

βύρσα.definition: skin stripped off, hide (prop. ox-hide; skin of a live animal, Theoc.25.238

βύσμα.definition: plug, bung, Hp.Mul.2.114 , Ar.Fr.299; Stilpo's stoppers, i. e. arguments with which he stopped his opponents' mouths, Diph.23

βωληνή.definition: a kind of vine grown in Bithynia, Gp.5.17.5

βωλίτης.definition: terrestrial fungus, Lat. boletus; root of Plin.HN21.171

βῶλος.definition: less freq. , lump, clod of; in Poets, land, soil, Mosch.4.37, cf. AP9.561 , etc.; Orac. ap. Plu.Flam.20, cf. Jul.Or.3.125b

βωμός.definition: raised platform, stand, for chariots; later, tomb, cairn, Epigr.Gr.319

βωσίον.definition: dub. sens. of a household utensil, Stud.Pal. 20.67

βαβράζω.definition: chatter, chirp, of the grasshopper, Anan.5.6

βάζω.definition: poet. Verb, used chiefly in pres. and impf.: aor. Hsch.: pf. Pass. :—speak, say, Il.14.92, al.; Od.4.837; Il.9.58; Od.18.168; Pi.Fr.157; AP7.636 : c. dupl. acc., Il.16.207, cf. E.Hipp.119; Id.Rh.719 ; A.Ch.882: c. dat…

βαθμίς.definition: base, pedestal, Pi.N.5.1; socket, Hp.Fract.2: generally, hollow in a joint, ib.37

βαθμός.definition: or step, threshold, LXXI; rung of a ladder, Luc.Trag.221

βαθύθριξ.definition: with thick, long mane, Opp.C.1.314; of sheep, with thick or long wool, h.Ap.412

βαθύκομος.definition: with thick leaves, covered with thick forests, Ar.Fr.698

βαθύνω.definition: —Pass., plpf. Nonn.D.39.305; Math., add a third dimension, Procl.in R.2.52 K., cf. in Ti.1.146 D.:—Pass., Simp.in Ph.59.17

βαθύπεδος.definition: with deep plain, lying low , of Nemea, Pi.N.3.18

βαίνω.definition: intr., walk, step, prop. of motion on foot, Il.5.745, etc.; but also of all motion on ground, the direction being commonly determined by a Prep.:—the kind of motion is often marked by a part., Il.2.665, 4.74: c. part.…

βακτρεύω.definition: support as a staff, of Antigone, Arg.metr.S.OC

βάλλω.definition: with acc. of person or thing aimed at, throw so as to hit, hit with a missile, freq. opp. striking with a weapon in the hand, Il.15.495; 11.350, cf. 4.473, al.; so even in . . 5.73; and 16.807; but later opp. D.9.17, …

βαμβαίνω.definition: onomatop. word, chatter with the teeth, Il.10.375; stammer, BionFr.6.9, AP5.272 , Procop.Arc.Praef.:—so also chatter with cold, Hippon.17:—also Phryn.PSp.54B., Hsch.; possibly to be restored in Arist.Pr.949a13

βάπτω.definition: trans., dip, . . Od.9.392; Pl.Ti.73e, cf. Emp.100.11; Ar.Ec.216; Arist.HA605a29, de An.435a2:—Pass., iron in process of being tempered, Plu.2.136a; and of coral, become hard, Dsc.5.121

βαρβαρίζω.definition: behave or speak like a barbarian; trans., 'murder', mangle, Luc.Merc.Cond.24

βαρέω.definition: Aeol. v. infr., fut. Luc.DMort.10.4: pf. D.C.78.17:-Pass., v. infr.:-weigh down, depress, Luc. l. c. ; Procop.Arc.14; Hermog.Inv.2.7; IG14.830.15 , cf. POxy. 1159.2 ; J.BJ2.14.1, cf. D.C. l. c.:-Pass., . . Sapph.Supp.…

βαρύθω.definition: to be weighed down; abs., to be heavy, AP7.481 ; . . A.R.1.43:—Pass., Max.212, Q.S.13.6

βαρύνω.definition: metaph., oppress, weary, Pi.P.1.84; X.Ap.9; of cold, Arist.Somn.Vig.456b26; make more grievous, Ph.2.425:— Pass., to be oppressed, distressed, Simon,184.5, Pi.N.7.43, S.El.820, Th.8.1; by calamities, A.Ag.836, cf. 189…

βαρύφρων.definition: gen. heavy of mind; weighty of purpose, grave-minded, Theoc.25.110

βαρύφωνος.definition: with a deep, bass voice, opp. Hp.Aër.6, Arist.GA786b7, etc

βαρυώδυνος.definition: suffering grievous pangs; causing grievous pangs, ib.48.808

βασιλεία.definition: Ion. kingdom, dominion; kingly office, Arist.Pol.1273a37

βασιλεύς.definition: of the gods, Hes.Th.886, cf. Pi.O.7.34, Emp.128.2, etc. ; as cult title of Zeus, IG7.3073.90 , SIG1014.110 , etc. ; of God, LXXPs.47.2, Ph.2.107: Sup. Max.Tyr.29.5

βασιλεύω.definition: to be king, rule, reign; to be at Athens, Isoc.18.5,IG12.776, al.; of other magistrates, SIG709 , 1054

βασίλη.definition: = queen, princess, S.Fr.310; a divinity, worshipped with Neleus and Codrus at Athens, IG12.94, Pl.Chrm.153a

βάσκανος.definition: one who bewitches, sorcerer, as a term; slanderer, D.18.132, Vett.Val.358.5

βάσκω.definition: only imper., speed thee! away! Il.2.8, etc.; Ar.Th.783; but come! A.Pers.663,671 ; Mim. Oxy.413.60

βαστάζω.definition: metaph., lift up, exalt, ennoble, Pi.O.12.19; Id.I.3.8; bear, carry, A.Pr.1019, etc.; S.El.1129, cf. 1216; Hermipp.46.2 , Theoc.16.78; Men.Epit.107

βάτης.definition: one that treads or covers, expld. by Id

βαΰζω.definition: trans., shriek aloud for, A.Pers.13; of dogs, bark at, Heraclit.97 codd

βαφεύς.definition: a dyer, Pl.R.429d, Diph.72; gilder, Zos.Alch.p.154B

βδελυρία.definition: beastly, coarse, or objectionable; disgust, nausea, Hp.Int.26, Jul.Or.6.190d

βδέω.definition: poet. aor. AP11.242 ; later; of the cockroach, Archig. ap. Aët.8.35, cf. Gal.12.861

βελουλκέω.definition: draw out darts, extracts the weapon (i.e. hook from itself, Plu.2.977b

βελουλκός.definition: instrument for drawing out darts, ibid

βέομαι.definition: and Homeric subj. used as fut., I shall live, Il.15.194; 16.852, cf. 24.131; 22.431. , whence should perh. be restored in Hom.)

βιάζω.definition: constrain, Act. once in Hom; Act., make good, suffice to discharge a debt, PFlor.56.13

βιβάσθω.definition: = only in part., long- striding, Il.13.809, 16.534

βιοτέρμων.definition: gen. marking the beginning of; lasting till the close of life, Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.110

βιόω.definition: Arist.HA558a20; Democr.200; survive, is found h.Ap.528 and 3pl. Orac. ap. Phleg.Mir.2, cf

βιώσκομαι.definition: causal of quicken, make or keep; later in pass. sensc, revive, Arist.Mete.351a35; simply, live, IG14.2100; Arr.Ind.9

βλαίσωσις.definition: metaph., retorting of a dilemma on its proposer, Arist.Rh.1399a26

βλακεύω.definition: to be slack, lazy, X.An.2.3.11, 5.8.15; c. acc., lose or waste through laziness, Luc.Ep.Sat.26

βλάπτω.definition: fut. E.Heracl.704, etc.: aor. Il.23.774: aor. 2 Q.S.5.509: pf. D.19.180, Plb.12.26.2, IG7.303.51 :-Pass., Isoc.1.25, Pl.Men.77e, Grg.475d, Hp.Mi.373a; Hp.Acut.16: also fut. Med. Th.1.81, 6.64: aor. 1 Il.16.331, etc.: …

βλεμεαίνω.definition: exult, of a lion, Il.12.42; of Hector, 8.337; cf

βλέπω.definition: Sol.11.8, etc.: impf. Batr.67: fut; look, S.Tr.402; Id.Aj.345 ; A.Pers.802; Th.7.71; D.18.283; with what face? S.Ph.110; ; Id.OT1371; Pl.Cra.428d: with Adv., X.Mem.3.10.4, Smp.4.58: freq. folld. by noun in acc., look …

βλιμάζω.definition: Lacon. feel hens to see if they; handle, treat, Aristeas188

βλίττω.definition: aor. Pl.R.564e:—cut out the comb of

βλύω.definition: = c. dat., Lyc.301: c. acc., Nonn.D.19.287: c. gen., OGI199.11. between two long syll. in Ep., A.R.3.223, cf. 4.1417.]

βόαρχος.definition: beginning with an ox, of a sacrifice in which an ox is the first victim, IG12.5

βοάω.definition: Ep. 3 sg. 3pl. part. Il.14.394, 17.265, 15.687: Ion.impf. A.R.2.588: fut. Th.7.48, etc.; Dor. Ar.Nu.1154 ; later A.R.3.792, AP7.32 , etc. is aor. subj.): aor. Il.11.15, S.Tr.772, etc.; Ep. Il.23.847; Dor. B.16.14; Ion…

βοηλασία.definition: driving of oxen, cattle-lifting; place where cattle are pastured, cattle-run, AP7.626

βόησις.definition: = cry, shout for assistance, Thd., Quint.Ps.21.2

βοθρίον.definition: Dim. of small trench, to set; small ulcer, Hp.Liqu.6

βοθρόω.definition: = Gal.8.951 ; of caries, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.22.1; of a tumor 'pitting' on pressure, Aët.15.1

βοίδης.definition: like an ox, quiet, stupid, Men.1002

βολέω.definition: = Theol.Ar.37, Eust.1405.4; in early; in literal sense, falling about his neck, A.R.1.262; . . dominated by Arcturus, Arat.609

βολίζω.definition: heave the lead, take soundings, Act.Ap.27.28, Eust.563.30:—Pass., sink in water, Gp.6.17

βομβέω.definition: make a booming noise; in Hom. always of falling bodies, Il.13.530; 16.118, cf. Od.18.397; . . the oars fell with a loud noise . . , 12.204; the stone flew humming through the air, 8.190; of the sea, roar, Simon.1; of …

βομβυλιός.definition: or buzzing insect: humble-; cocoon of the silk-worm , Arist.HA551b12

βοόκτιτος.definition: of Thebes, founded where the heifer lay, Nonn.D.25.415

βορρόλιψ.definition: north-west wind, PMag.Par.1.1646, Ptol.Tetr.60:—hence Adj. north-western, ib.39

βοσκάς.definition: of birds which feed themselves, not artificially fed, Aët.9.30

βόσκω.definition: impf. Ep. Il.15.548: fut; prop. of herdsmen, feed, tend, Od.14.102; Stratt.27; the feeder, Arist.HA540a18

βουβῆτις.definition: stream for watering cattle, Tab. Herad.2.13

βουγονής.definition: born of an ox, of bees, Gp.15.2.14; ibid. tit. is perh. f.l. for title of poem by Eumelus, Varro RR 2.5.5

βουθύτης.definition: name given to Pythagoras, Procl.in Euc.p.426F

βούθυτος.definition: of or belonging to sacrifices, esp. of

βουκολέω.definition: tend cattle, (Ep; c. acc. rei, graze on, Euph.114

βουλεύω.definition: abs., Il.1.531; in council or in battle, Od.14.491; 9.420, cf. 11.229; 16.234; we shall agree to one plan, Il.2.379; Od.12.58; Hdt.1.120, Th.3.28, 5.116: in Prose, chiefly Med. in this sense, v. infr. B

βουληγόρος.definition: one who speaks in the Senate, ib.25

βουλητέος.definition: to be wished for; one must wish for, Id.Rh.Al.1420b23

βούλομαι.definition: in Hom. of gods, c. acc. rei et dat. pers., . . he willed victory to the Trojans, Il.7.21, cf. 23.682: later c. acc., that supports the constitution, Arist.Pol.1309b17

βούνομος.definition: grazed by cattle, of pastures, A.Fr.249; herds of grazing oxen, Id.OT26

βουφόνος.definition: ox-slaying, h.Merc.436; at or for which steers are slain, A.Pr.531

βοώνης.definition: at Athens, an officer who bought oxen for the sacrifices, D.21.171, IG2.163.18

βοωτία.definition: arable land or ploughing, Crito Hist.3

βόωψ.definition: small fish with large eyes, Ar.Byz. ap. Ath.7.287a. .)

βραβεῖον.definition: Ep. prize in the games; wand, baton given as a prize, CIG3674 , cf.IG14.748

βράσσω.definition: Att. aor. Hp.Ep.23; abs., = boil, interpol. in Gp.7.15.20; dub. sens. in Hp. l.c

βρέμω.definition: only pres. and impf. (aor. vv.ll; after Hom., of arms, clash, ring, E.Heracl.832; of men, clamour, rage, A.Pr.424 , cf. Th.378; E.Ph.113; against one, Id.HF962; of a mob, A.Eu.978 ; murmur, grumble, Pi.P.11.30; wail, …

βρεφόω.definition: form into a foetus, engender, Eust.1535.44:—Pass., Theol.Ar.6

βριάω.definition: make strong and mighty, Hes.Th.447; intr., to be strong, Opp.H.5.96: in both senses, Hes.Op.5

βρίθω.definition: Ep. subj. Od.19.112: Ep. impf; c. gen., to be laden with or full of, Od.15.334; S.Fr.286; Ph.2.217

βρίμη.definition: strength, might, h.Hom.28.10, A.R.4.1677; bellowing, roaring, prob. in Orph.Fr.79

βρογχία.definition: Ion. imaginary system of ducts connecting heart with liver, Hp.Anat.1

βρομέω.definition: = only used in pres. and impf. ; of flies, buzz, Il.16.642; of wind, roar, A.R.4.787, cf. Nic.Al.596; of boiling broth, Id.Fr.68.5; also of a proud person, Rhian.1.13

βροντάω.definition: impers., it thunders, Ar.Fr.46; if it thunders, Arist.HA610b35

βροντή.definition: the state of one struck with thunder, astonishment

βροτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be stained with gore, Od.11.41, Q.S.1.717; Stesich.42

βροχθίζω.definition: take a mouthful, Arist.Pr.948a5; clear the throat, with . . , Clearch.Com.2

βρυχάομαι.definition: aor. Ep. A.R.4.19, Max.Tyr.31.3, D.C.68.24, Pl.Phd.117d; also : Ep. pf. Od.5.412, al.: plpf. 12.242:—onomatop. Verb, roar, bellow, prop. of lions, acc. to Hsch. and Ammon.; of a bull, S.Aj.322, cf. Ar.Ra.823; of wild …

βρυχηθμός.definition: roaring, of the sea or a river; gnashing of teeth, lamentation, Men.Epit.472

βρυχητήρ.definition: roarer, of the constellation Leo, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.36

βρυχιάω.definition: chatter , of a defect of speech, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.167

βρύω.definition: mostly pres.: impf., Pherecyd.Syr. ap; c. dat., swell or teem with, esp. of plants, . . swells with white bloom, Il.17.56, cf. E.Ba.107 ; Eub.56.6; Philostr.Her.2.2, Alciphr.3.31, Luc.Am.12; Arist.Mu.392b15; also B.3.…

βυρσόω.definition: cover with skins or leather, Ath.Mech.12.10, al

βυσσοδομεύω.definition: build in the deep: hence, brood over a thing in the depth of one's soul, ponder deeply; Hom. only in Od., always in bad sense, 17.66, al.; 4.676; Hes.Sc.30: also in late Prose, Luc.Cal.24; secret designs, Hld.7.11:—al…

βύω.definition: c. gen. rei, stuff full of, only in Pass., stuffed full of spun-work or spinning, Od.4.134; Hdt.6.125; Nonn.D.9.298

βωθέω.definition: Ion. contr. for v.l. in Hdt.8.47

βωλάκιος.definition: lumpy, loamy, opp. dry sandy soil, Pi.P.4.228

βωστρέω.definition: call on, esp. call to aid, Od.12.124, cf. Ar.Pax1146, al., Theoc.5.64; cry after, . . Mosch.1.1; Opp.C.4.293: abs., of birds, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.7.8
